# Gemini

*Product* · also written Gemini app · Gemini apps · Gemini models

Google's family of AI models and the assistant app built on them; Gemini models also power AI features in Search and Google Trends.

Narrative: the topic [Gemini and Search](../topics/gemini-and-search.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

41 claims mention it: 7 from Google's documentation, 25 shown or said at the event (10 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 12 consistent with Google docs, 2 nothing to verify), 9 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [A new era of intelligence with Gemini 3](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-3/), [Grounding with Google Search](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search).

- [`D1-C086`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Docs: Google-Extended is a control token, not a crawler with its own user agent string. It decides whether crawled content may be used to train future Gemini models and to ground Gemini apps and Vertex AI. `[D1-C086, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers]`
- [`D2-C121`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google's crawler documentation defines grounding in Gemini Apps and in Grounding with Google Search on Vertex AI as providing content from the Google Search index to the model at prompt time, and sites manage whether their content is used for it with the Google-Extended robots.txt token. `[D2-C121, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers]`
- [`D2-C122`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Docs: Google says user-triggered fetchers, which fetch a URL because a user asked for it in a Google product (for example Gemini Notebook fetching URLs users add as sources, or Google-Agent acting on a user's request), generally ignore robots.txt rules. `[D2-C122, docs, Google, https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-user-triggered-fetchers]`
- [`D2-C771`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Docs: Google announced Nano Banana, a new image editing model from Google DeepMind in the Gemini app, on 26 August 2025. `[D2-C771, docs, Google blog (26 August 2025), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/updated-image-editing-model/]`
- [`D3-C094`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Docs: Google's Gemini API documentation on grounding with Google Search says the model automatically generates and runs one or more search queries when needed, and the response lists the search queries it executed. `[D3-C094, docs, Google AI for Developers (Gemini API docs), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search]`
- [`D3-C361`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Docs: On 11 January 2026 Google announced 'dozens of new data attributes' in Merchant Center for conversational commerce on AI Mode, Gemini and Business Agent, to roll out first with a small group of retailers. `[D3-C361, docs, Google blog (11 January 2026), https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/agentic-commerce-ai-tools-protocol-retailers-platforms/]`
- [`D3-C712`](../sessions/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) Docs: Google's July 2025 blog post introduced Web Guide as a Search Labs experiment that uses a custom version of Gemini and a query fan-out technique to group web links by aspects of the query. `[D3-C712, docs, Google blog (24 July 2025), https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/web-guide-labs/]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C162`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Google said that after the launch of Nano Banana, its image generation model, the Gemini app became the number one app in the app store in 2025. `[D1-C162, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C335`](../sessions/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Crawling for Gemini may be set to care less about quality and more about the amount of content, because for large language models the number of tokens matters more than quality. `[D1-C335, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C118`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: To train Gemini models, Google renders every page just as it does for Search, so a page that renders correctly for Search also works for Gemini training, provided the site allows its content to be used for training. `[D2-C118, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C120`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: When a Gemini user asks about a specific web page (for example, whether it says anything about the ruby HTML tag), the page is read at that moment rather than during crawling and may be used to ground the answer, which takes extra time. `[D2-C120, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C325`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Tokenization for AI models such as Gemini, in training and in inference, differs from tokenization for Search, although Gary Illyes qualified this with 'or mostly'. `[D2-C325, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C825`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Gary Illyes added that, once chunk size is thought of in millions of tokens as Gemini's context window allows, chunking has perhaps lost its meaning anyway. `[D2-C825, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C669`](../sessions/D2-S19-calculating-some-signals.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: SpamBrain, Google's AI-based spam detection system, is nowadays built on Gemini and fine-tuned specifically for finding spam. `[D2-C669, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C769`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: A Google Trends Explore chart presented on stage put worldwide search interest in Gemini above ChatGPT for the first time ever in September 2025, during a sharp surge for Gemini. `[D2-C769, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C770`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google attributed the September 2025 surge in worldwide search interest for Gemini to the viral launch of Nano Banana (the image editing model in the Gemini app), as people searched for both Gemini and Nano Banana. `[D2-C770, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C773`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: After the Nano Banana surge faded, worldwide baseline search interest in Gemini stayed much higher than before, which Google read as a sustained gain in brand recognition. `[D2-C773, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C163`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google described a full-stack approach to AI, from its own TPU chips for AI inference through research and frontier models such as Gemini to its apps. `[D1-C163, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C172`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said the Gemini model lets Search understand the user's intent, and query fan-out then adds further queries to the first one to enrich the quality of the answer. `[D1-C172, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C496`](../sessions/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said that last year (2025) it delivered a decade of innovation in 12 months, with its new Gemini model at the top of all the benchmarks. `[D1-C496, stage, Lino Cattaruzzi, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C039`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Slide, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Gemini is not part of Search, but it uses crawlers for data, shares some technologies such as tokenization and deduping, and grounds on the Search index. `[D1-C039, slide, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C522`](../sessions/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said a site can keep a directory or the whole site out of Gemini model training by disallowing it for the Google-Extended token in robots.txt, and that Google respects that policy; the speaker believed Google was the first to offer such an opt-out from model training. `[D1-C522, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C117`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: AI Overviews and AI Mode typically do not ground their answers by reading pages live, unlike Gemini when a user asks about a specific page, Google said. `[D2-C117, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C331`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Gary Illyes said Gemini's context window, where chunking actually matters, holds millions of tokens. `[D2-C331, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C332`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Gemini does not need content cut into small chunks of 100 or 200 words, Gary Illyes said, since a smaller book fits in its context window. `[D2-C332, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C869`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Right after saying Gemini's context window holds millions of tokens, Gary Illyes put its size at perhaps 900,000 or even closer to a million, without a unit that the recordings capture. `[D2-C869, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C465`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Gemini in Chrome relies heavily on the screenshot it takes of a page. `[D2-C465, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C808`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google Trends' Suggest search terms combines Gemini's knowledge of the world with Google Trends data. `[D2-C808, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C064`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Individual fan-out queries can be seen in some other places, such as Gemini, some search APIs and other LLM systems. `[D3-C064, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C419`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Query groups can change when the meaning of a query changes over time: a 2023 search for 'Gemini' may have meant the astrological sign, but after Google launched Gemini it means something else, so Search Console may now group it differently. `[D3-C419, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C951`](../sessions/D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: A community speaker named the limits of the title-based alt-text script: it rewrites only the hero image, assumes the page title states the user's intent, had been tested in only one language or market, and runs on the free Gemini model. `[D2-C951, stage, a community speaker, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C187`](../sessions/D3-S05-how-google-thinks-about-quality.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's quality talk showed a surface-level example article (not photographed) that the speaker said Gemini could have generated, while stressing that humans have written such content for a long time too. `[D3-C187, stage, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C486`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Analysis: The panel spoke of blocking Google's 'AI crawling or training' with Google-Extended, but Google documents Google-Extended as a usage token, not a crawler: disallowing it does not stop Googlebot fetching pages and only controls use for Gemini training and grounding. `[D1-C486, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C067`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: nofollow is a link-graph hint for search engines, not an access control: to keep AI crawlers away from content, use robots.txt rules for the specific crawlers; at Google, Google-Extended covers Gemini training and grounding, and the Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews and AI Mode. `[D2-C067, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C119`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: If Gemini training reuses the rendering done for Search, a site needs no separate rendering work for Gemini; whether its rendered content is used for training is decided with the Google-Extended token in robots.txt, not by rendering choices. `[D2-C119, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C123`](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) Analysis: Google documents Gemini grounding only as content from the Search index at prompt time; the live read of a specific page at a user's request, described on stage, is not documented, so it is unclear whether it works like a user-triggered fetcher, which generally ignores robots.txt, or follows Google-Extended. `[D2-C123, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C329`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Day 1's slide said Gemini shares technologies such as tokenization with Search, while on Day 2 Gary Illyes showed that the two tokenizers split the same text differently ('or mostly'); read this as a shared processing step with different outputs, so Search's word tokens and Gemini's sub-word tokens are not the same units. `[D2-C329, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C333`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: Do not rewrite pages into short, self-contained chunks for AI systems; Google says Gemini reads context windows of millions of tokens, so structure content for readers, with clear headings and complete explanations. `[D2-C333, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C872`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Analysis: The talk gave Gemini's context window both as millions of tokens and as roughly 900,000 to a million; Google's long-context docs say Gemini models have context windows of 1 million or more tokens (about eight average novels per million), so plan with about one million tokens as the documented floor rather than several million. `[D2-C872, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C772`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Analysis: On stage the Nano Banana launch was placed in September 2025, but Google announced it on 26 August 2025, so the September 2025 surge in Gemini search interest described in the talk came in the weeks after the launch. `[D2-C772, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C066`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Analysis: Do not build pages for fan-out queries copied from Gemini or other LLM tools: they differ from system to system and Search Console does not report them. Cover a topic's real subquestions on solid pages instead. `[D3-C066, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
